title: Stop Overpaying at Nigerian Motor Parks: Inside the Intercityprices VIP Group (2026)
excerpt: Tired of surprise park price hikes, broken AC buses, and touts? See how 82+ Nigerian travellers use the Intercityprices VIP WhatsApp Group to get live terminal-to-terminal fares before leaving home.
content:
If you travel by road in Nigeria, you already know the routine: you budget based on what a friend paid last month, arrive at the park at 6:30 AM, and suddenly discover the fare has jumped by ₦7,000—or worse, you pay for an 'AC Sienna' only to sweat through Lokoja with the windows down.

Between fluctuating fuel costs and seasonal rushes, guessing transport prices before leaving your house is an expensive mistake. That is the exact problem the Intercityprices VIP WhatsApp Group was built to solve.

What Actually Happens Inside the VIP Group?

Instead of relying on outdated price lists or smooth-talking park touts, the VIP group connects 82+ active Nigerian travellers and verified route agents in one live WhatsApp community. Here is what members get access to before they book a ticket:

1. Direct Admin & Verified Agent Q&A

Need to know "How much is Uyo to Warri right now?" or which park in Abuja has the fastest departure to Makurdi? Drop your route in the chat and get real terminal-to-terminal answers from verified agents before you leave your house.

2. Cheapest Travel Day Alerts

Transport fares on major corridors don't stay flat all week. Members get timely alerts on when prices dip (such as mid-week Tuesday and Wednesday windows) and which peak days to avoid travelling.

3. Unfiltered Traveller Reviews (AC, Safety & Delays)

Brochures won't tell you which operator's buses have been breaking down or whose AC actually works. Fellow travellers share honest, real-time feedback on which companies to book and which ones to avoid.

4. Live Road & Terminal Updates

Find out about heavy gridlock, security checkpoints, or long boarding queues at major terminals like Jibowu, Utako, or Mile 1 while you are still at home.

Is the ₦1,000 Monthly Access Worth It?

Let's do simple math. On routes like Lagos to Abuja, Abuja to Calabar, or Port Harcourt to Lagos, a single bad booking decision—or paying a tout's inflated park rate—easily costs you ₦3,000 to ₦10,000 extra.

At ₦1,000 per month, saving just once on a single trip pays for the membership three to ten times over—and keeps you from getting stranded at an unfamiliar terminal.

Who Should Join?

  • Frequent Interstate Travellers & Business Owners: Anyone moving regularly between Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, the East, or the North who wants accurate terminal-to-terminal rates.
  • Solo Travellers & Students: Travellers who want verified safety feedback and direct agent answers before heading to a park.
  • Holiday & Festive Season Travellers: Anyone planning trips during high-demand surges who wants to know the cheapest days to move.
